gameStory.articleHeadline: Brock Purdy leads 2 late scoring drives to deliver a 32-29 win for the 49ers over the Seahawks
gameStory.articleDescription: — When the game was on the line and San Francisco's struggling offense needed to move the ball, Mike Evans stepped up and showed why the 49ers went after him so hard this offseason.
gameStory.articleStory: SEATTLE -- — When the game was on the line and San Francisco's struggling offense needed to move the ball, Mike Evans stepped up and showed why the 49ers went after him so hard this offseason. Purdy found Evans repeatedly on the go-ahead touchdown drive and then led the Niners down the field again for a 43-yard field goal by Eddy Pineiro with 1:56 to play that gave San Francisco a 32-29 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday in a playoff rematch. The win for the 49ers (5-0) offered a small bit of payback for their two late-season losses to Seattle (3-2) last season, including a 41-6 defeat in the divisional round of the playoffs with a short-handed roster. San Francisco was healthier on defense for the first meeting this season, and also had Evans after signing him in March. That was a big reason why Purdy was able to deliver late for the undefeated Niners. “He's a game changer,” Purdy said. “True X receiver that if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. whatToWatch.text: Defense vs. defense, and Seattle's got the edge: the 3-1 Hawks are giving up just 18.25 points a game, but the Niners are stingier at 16.0 — and that 46.5 total says Vegas expects a grinder at the Clink.
The pass rush is the difference-maker: Seattle's getting home 2.75 times a game to San Francisco's 1.5. If that gap holds up, the home crowd gets exactly the kind of afternoon it shows up for.

Both sides are banged up — four Seahawks out (Julian Neal, Irv Charles, Chazz Surratt) and one questionable, with four Niners out including James Thompson Jr. and Upton Stout. Seattle's a 3-point home favorite riding a one-game win streak, so depth and discipline decide this one.

recap.text: Seattle built a 26-21 edge behind five Jason Myers field goals and a 16-yard Sam Darnold strike to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but four giveaways — including a fumble San Francisco's Gracen Halton pounced on in the end zone — kept the 49ers alive all afternoon. Brock Purdy then took the game over late, hitting Brandin Cooks from seven yards out and finding Mike Evans for two to flip the lead. Myers answered with a 40-yarder to even it, only for Eddy Pineiro to boot a 44-yard winner inside the final two minutes. Seattle's last gasp died when a third-down throw slipped through Smith-Njigba's hands near midfield, sealing a 32-29 loss.

newsBlurb.text: Divisional football returns to Lumen Field when San Francisco visits for a Week 5 Sunday showdown. The 49ers get the full Seattle treatment — crowd noise, a hostile October afternoon, and a rivalry that rarely needs extra motivation. Kickoff details, TV, radio and streaming info are all set for October 11.
